claim_text: AP and index alpha are related but distinct objectives.
rationale: AP/AUC/R@FPR are label-ranking diagnostics; alpha is portfolio realized return after thresholding and weighting.

claim_text: Higher AP mechanically implies higher alpha.
rationale: OOS AP vs total-market alpha Pearson r is -0.042425 and Spearman rho is -0.100870 across 24 completed/reused CMT runs.

claim_text: The AP winner is the total-market alpha winner.
rationale: AP winner C060_M000_T012 differs from total-market alpha winner C090_M020_T018.

claim_text: The main CMT run is not an outlier.
rationale: Main run C080_M020_T018 sits inside the sensitivity distribution; below median total/large cap and above median mid/small cap.

claim_text: Fixed-FPR recall appears more aligned with alpha than AP in the CMT sample.
rationale: R@FPR3 has Pearson r 0.336036 versus AP Pearson r -0.042425, but relationship remains moderate and non-deterministic.

claim_text: Model metrics alone can select the final index-construction rule.
rationale: Threshold, lockout, market-cap weighting, timing, error-cost composition, turnover, and costs mediate portfolio outcomes.

claim_text: Temporary-CSI sensitivity supports robustness rather than replacing the headline setup.
rationale: Main run is not outlier; different objectives select different CMT settings.

claim_text: The same CMT sensitivity conclusions apply to permanent CSI.
rationale: Permanent-CSI CMT sensitivity remains unavailable/future work.
Correlations are descriptive diagnostics over 24 completed/reused sensitivity runs and model-suite family summaries.

claim_text: Transaction costs are the main explanation for AP-alpha divergence.
rationale: Transaction cost drag is economically visible but smaller than variation from CMT setting, threshold, lockout, and universe choice.
